hero.title: A research atlas for civil-resistance methods and agent skills.
hero.lead: Civil Resistance Skills turns public method taxonomies into a source-linked atlas for study, simulation, and careful preparation with AI agents.
hero.boundary: This is research, education, simulation, and planning infrastructure. It is not a campaign organizer. Higher-risk methods remain descriptive records for analysis rather than operational guidance.

atlas.kicker: Civic Research Atlas / 347 methods / 6 domains / risk-reviewed AI skills

notes.title: Applied examples: 4104-public-speeches / 4004-marches
notes.body: Each published skill includes phases, working artifacts, review checks, and readiness criteria.

notes.title: Higher-risk records: 54 kept for education and simulation
notes.body: Applied guidance depends on sources, legality, safety, and explicit review.

why.title: Why this exists
why.body: Civil-resistance methods are often published as prose taxonomies. AI agents need a clearer structure: source provenance, risk boundaries, availability, references, and completion criteria.

cards.title: Source basis
cards.body: The atlas crosswalks the Beer/NVI/ICNC tactic universe with Sharp's method taxonomy. Primary sources identify methods; secondary training sources inform low-risk preparation patterns.

cards.title: Risk-reviewed transformation
cards.body: Low-risk methods can become applied skills with planning, research, review, and debrief support. Higher-risk methods stay descriptive for education, analysis, and simulation until explicitly reviewed.

cards.title: For whom
cards.body: For researchers, civic educators, agent builders, simulation designers, movement-support analysts, and careful practitioners who need structured learning rather than slogans.

cards.title: Simulation path
cards.body: Skills are shaped as structured artifacts: phases, outputs, checks, risk flags, and readiness judgments. That makes them useful for future sandbox and game agents.

install.title: Install options
install.body: The canonical skills live in this repository. Claude Code and Codex use separate plugin surfaces so each agent can discover skills in its native format.
install.claudeBody: Add the marketplace, then install the communication plugin.
install.codexBody: Add the Codex marketplace, then choose plugins from the native plugin UI.

domainsSection.title: Domains
domainsSection.body: Six domains organize the 347 methods. Communication is the first active domain; the others remain indexed and planned until applied skills are authored.

catalog.title: Method atlas
catalog.body: Implemented rows link to published skill files. Planned rows are indexed methods not yet turned into skills. Higher-risk rows remain analysis-only.

footer.text: Civil Resistance Skills - research and simulation infrastructure.

hero.title: Communication, symbols, media, and public narrative.
hero.lead: This is the first active domain. Its applied skills focus on low-risk communication methods that can be prepared, reviewed, simulated, and debriefed without turning the atlas into a campaign command system.

operational.title: Applied skills
operational.body: These are the current example skills. They use source-linked references, working phases, artifacts, risk review, and readiness criteria.

skills.title: Public Speeches
skills.body: Helps prepare a public speech method. Planning Mode produces a research-backed speech brief; Application Mode can produce a complete speech package.

skills.title: Marches
skills.body: Planning-only skill for a march planning package: route, legal posture, staffing, safety, accessibility, communications, debrief criteria, and readiness judgment.

registry.title: Communication registry
registry.body: All communication methods remain visible so the research surface is complete. Rows without skill files are marked planned; higher-risk rows stay analysis-only.

communication.footer: Civil Resistance Skills - communication domain atlas.
